price_growth.source: Realised price growth FY2026E-FY2030E, NOMINAL EGP per tonne. Every year is a REAL price DECLINE: nominal growth of 4.5-6.0% against CBE inflation of ~16% in 2026 easing toward 7% then 5%. That is the supply-glut thesis expressed in the price line — seven to nine dormant lines are under study for revival, potentially adding 12.6Mt from 2H-2026, about 23% of 2025 domestic consumption, landing inside the forecast window

ebitda_mgn.source: EBITDA margin FY2026E-FY2030E, gliding DOWN from the derived FY2025 cyclical peak. Two named, dated mechanisms: the 12.6Mt capacity revival and Egypt's phased energy-subsidy reform, which raises the local energy bill independent of the global fuel price. The FY2030E terminal margin of 26.0% sits ABOVE the FY2024 outturn of 24.8% and well BELOW the FY2025 peak — a mid-cycle, not a peak, perpetuity

dna_pct.source: Depreciation and amortisation as a share of revenue. The El Hassana plant commissioned from 1997 and is substantially written down, so the charge is modest against a revenue base inflated by EGP devaluation; it declines as a percentage as nominal revenue outgrows the historic-cost asset base

capex_pct.source: Capex as a share of revenue. NO capital-expenditure figure, guidance or investment programme is disclosed in any retrievable source (logged as a dated negative search), so this is a top-down setting: maintenance capex for a mature, fully built two-line plant plus decarbonisation spending (alternative fuels, clinker factor), benchmarked slightly above the D&A charge so the asset base is maintained in real terms

wc_pct_drev.source: Change in working capital as a share of the change in revenue. Cement is a low-working-capital business — bulk product, short receivable cycle, no long contracts — so growth absorbs little cash

payout.source: Dividend payout ratio from FY2026E. Vicat-controlled, net cash, no announced expansion programme and no meaningful reinvestment need, so the cash is upstreamed. Affects the cash build and therefore the bridge, not FCFF

cash_yield.source: Yield earned on the cash balance FY2026E-FY2030E, following the CBE easing path down from the 19.50% main operation rate held since 2 April 2026 toward the norm-built terminal

cash_growth_fy25.source: FY2025 closing cash as a multiple of FY2024 closing cash. FY2025 generated EGP 2.29bn of profit against modest capex and no disclosed distribution, so the balance builds; 1.35x is struck below the ratio a full retention would give, allowing for the distribution the equity roll-forward implies

cash_yield_fy25.source: Average yield earned on cash through FY2025, when the CBE main operation rate ran 24.00% to 21.00%

beta.source: ADOPTED beta 1.00 — tier-3 default on a GENUINE usability-gate failure, disclosed with the diagnostics that triggered it. The tier-1 own-stock weekly regression against a 32-name equal-weight EGX composite (5-year window, SCEM excluded from its own index) returns beta 0.485 with R-squared 0.038, n=256, standard error 0.153 — R-squared below the 0.05 floor, so the regression is NOT usable. Tier-2 is unavailable: no Egyptian listed cement peer carries an OHLC series in the engine library. 1.00 is corroborated, not arbitrary: it sits inside the Dimson sum-beta 90% interval [0.35, 1.32] and at the bottom of the 1.0-1.5 cyclical-materials prior, the discount being explained by the company carrying no financial leverage

kd.source: Marginal pre-tax cost of debt. The company borrows in Egyptian pounds only and has essentially no debt (EGP 36.8mn, 0.17% of capital employed at market), so no effective rate can be computed from disclosure — neither interest expense nor an opening/closing debt schedule is retrievable, logged as a dated negative search. Set at the CBE main operation rate of 19.50% plus a 200bp corporate spread. The Kd-integrity gate cannot be satisfied on evidence here, so its materiality is COMPUTED instead and published: see kd_immaterial

kd_path.source: Forward cost-of-debt path FY2026E-FY2030E, following the CBE easing cycle toward the 7% (2026) and 5% (2028) inflation targets. The WACC glide takes its SHAPE from this path by construction rather than being invented separately

kd_term.source: Terminal cost of debt: the Egyptian long-run corporate-borrowing norm of 14-16%, midpoint 15%, with no name-specific reason to deviate

rf_term.source: Terminal risk-free rate, NORM-BUILT: the CBE's own stated medium-term inflation target of 5% plus the standard ~5.5pp emerging-market real-rate convention. Never a raw historical average, never reverse-engineered from a price

erp_term.source: Terminal equity risk premium, normalised BELOW the currently elevated crisis-era level toward the rating-class norm; never held flat into perpetuity

wd_term.source: Terminal debt weight D/(D+E), NORMALISED rather than today's ~0%. A mature cement producer in steady state carries some structural debt even if this one currently carries none

g_term.source: Terminal growth 5% — the standing centre for established names in this market post-disinflation, sensitised 3-7%. This is an EGP-NOMINAL rate struck against a terminal risk-free rate that itself embeds 5% inflation, so the base case assumes approximately ZERO real terminal growth — deliberate conservatism for a single-plant producer facing a supply glut

ev_ebitda_just.source: Justified EV/EBITDA on mid-cycle earnings. Anchored on the named Egyptian peer: Misr Beni Suef trades at 5.03x EV/EBITDA and 6.44x trailing earnings. 5.0x is struck at the peer, with no premium for SCEM's net cash (which the bridge already adds separately) and no discount for its 22.4% float — the float discount is disclosed qualitatively rather than double-counted in the multiple

pe_just.source: Justified price/earnings on normalised earnings. Above the 6.44x peer trailing multiple because the normalised base already strips the cyclical peak, so the same multiple applied to a lower base would double-count the cycle

norm_mgn.source: Mid-cycle EBITDA margin for the normalised-earnings lens: the midpoint of the FY2024 trough-to-recovery outturn (24.8%) and the FY2025 peak (derived 31.9%), rounded to 26.5% and cross-checked against the FY2030E terminal margin of 26.0%

ev_t_just.source: Justified enterprise value per annual tonne of capacity, USD 95/t.Below the USD 130/t replacement cost because SCEM runs at ~71% utilisation in a market carrying 76Mt of nameplate capacity against 54Mt of consumption — nobody pays replacement cost for capacity in a glut — and above a distressed level because the plant is operating, profitable and cash-generative

Weighted central.basis: the weighted blend across the four lens ranges

experts.label: Expert 1
experts.summary: Values the company as an asset, not an earnings stream. A 3.8Mt grey-cement plant costs roughly USD 130 per annual tonne to build; nobody pays replacement cost for capacity in a market carrying 76Mt against 54Mt of consumption, so the justified figure is USD 95/t. The market is paying USD 81/t. On this view the shares are cheap against steel and concrete in the ground, and the cycle is somebody else's problem.
experts.falsifier: Find a recent Egyptian cement line built, bought or restarted for less than USD 95 per annual tonne, or evidence that the El Hassana lines need major refurbishment capex. Either would collapse the asset floor. The 12.6Mt revival programme is the live test: restarting a dormant line costs far less per tonne than building one.

experts.label: Expert 2
experts.summary: Refuses to capitalise a peak. 2025 was the first year since 2008 that Egypt's supply-demand gap closed, prices roughly doubled and utilisation hit 98% — none of which is a plateau. Normalises the margin to 26.5%, between the FY2024 outturn and the FY2025 peak, and applies 7x. Concludes the market is extrapolating a cyclical high.
experts.falsifier: Two consecutive years of realised prices holding above EGP 3,900/t WITH the revival programme proceeding would prove the mid-cycle margin too low and this lens too bearish. Equally, a cancelled revival programme plus continued 13% demand growth would make 26.5% the new floor rather than the middle.

experts.label: Expert 3
experts.summary: Starts from the balance sheet. Net cash of EGP 5.3bn is 37% of the market capitalisation, and the operating business throws off roughly EGP 1931mn of free cash flow a year against essentially no reinvestment need — terminal return on capital of 9.4% is below the 16.3% cost of capital, so growth destroys value and the right policy is to harvest and distribute. Capitalises mid-cycle free cash flow at an 18% required yield and adds the cash.
experts.falsifier: The whole lens rests on the cash being distributable. If no dividend is declared on FY2026 profits, or the cash is deployed into a capacity expansion into a glutted market, the cash is worth materially less than face and this lens is wrong. The unexplained gap between rolled-forward and reported FY2025 equity — about EGP 1.9bn — is the first place to look, because it may already be a distribution nobody has reported.

growth_destroys_value.note: Terminal ROIC 9.4% is BELOW terminal WACC 16.3%, so higher terminal growth LOWERS fair value. Any driver test asserting the conventional direction for g would be asserting the wrong expectation.

assert_log: SCEM — Sinai Cement Company S.A.E. (EGX: SCEM) — computation log

[Share count] three independent methods: issued capital 260.812mn | tender-offer back-solve 260.789mn | market cap / close 260.789mn -> mean 260.797mn, spread 0.0091%. Adopted 260.812477mn (the issued-capital figure, a legal fact).
[Market] spot EGP 79.00 x 260.812mn shares = market capitalisation EGP 20,604mn. Vicat's tender offer at EGP 41.00 is -48.1% against spot.
[FY2024 base reset] Sinai White disposal: EUR 30mn x EGP 53.4/EUR = EGP 1,602mn proceeds, less an estimated EGP 100mn carrying value = EGP 1,502mn gain.
[FY2024 P&L closure] EBITDA 1,590 (disclosed) less D&A 398 = EBIT 1,192; profit after tax 3,070 less the disposal gain 1,502, grossed up at 22.5%, implies treasury income of 831.
[FY2025 P&L closure] profit after tax 2,290 grossed up at 22.5% = pre-tax 2,955; less treasury income 831 = EBIT 2,124; plus D&A 418 = EBITDA 2,542, a 28.0% margin.
[FY2023 P&L closure] net loss -121.4 less treasury income 198 = EBIT -319; plus D&A 402 = EBITDA 83, a 1.9% margin — the quota-era trough.

[The reframe] FY2024 profit EXCLUDING the disposal gain is EGP 1,568mn. Against FY2025's 2,290, underlying profit ROSE +46% — it did not fall 25%. The headline decline is an artefact of the FY2024 gain.
[Unit build] volume x realised price reproduces disclosed revenue by construction:
FY2023: 2.02Mt (53.2% of 3.8Mt capacity) x EGP 2,118/t = EGP 4,280mn
FY2024: 2.38Mt (62.6% of 3.8Mt capacity) x EGP 2,697/t = EGP 6,420mn
FY2025: 2.70Mt (71.1% of 3.8Mt capacity) x EGP 3,367/t = EGP 9,090mn
[Forecast] revenue EGP 9,732mn -> 13,069mn, a 7.5% CAGR against ~8% average inflation — roughly flat in REAL terms, which is the supply-glut thesis.

[Cost of equity] rf 22.31% less sovereign CDS spread 3.40% = 18.91%; + beta 1.00 x ERP 9.41% -> Ke 28.32%. The retired un-netted construction would give 31.72%, 340bp higher — that gap is the sovereign double-count this procedure removes.
[WACC explicit] weights: debt 0.178%, equity 99.822% (the company is net cash, so this is an almost pure equity cost) -> WACC 28.30%
[WACC terminal] Ke 17.50% (norm-built rf 10.50% + beta x ERP 7.00%); Kd after tax 11.62%; normalised weights 80%/20% -> terminal WACC 16.32%

[Kd integrity — cannot be satisfied on evidence, so materiality is COMPUTED] A +/-700bp error in Kd moves the WACC by 1.93bp in total, because debt is 0.178% of the capital structure. The gate's purpose — protecting the input the valuation is most convex to — is not engaged here: this valuation is essentially not a function of Kd at all.
[Discount schedule] glide fractions from kd_path: [0.0, 0.364, 0.636, 0.855, 1.0]
FY2026E: forward WACC 28.30%  cumulative discount factor 0.7794
FY2027E: forward WACC 23.94%  cumulative discount factor 0.6289
FY2028E: forward WACC 20.68%  cumulative discount factor 0.5211
FY2029E: forward WACC 18.07%  cumulative discount factor 0.4414
FY2030E: forward WACC 16.32%  cumulative discount factor 0.3794
[DCF waterfall] (EGP mn)
FY2026E    FY2027E    FY2028E    FY2029E    FY2030E
[Terminal growth — historical reconciliation]
Year        Capex  Cx/EBITDA  Character    NOPAT     ROIC       RR  ROICxRR
Check (a) actual NOPAT growth FY2024->FY2025: +78.2% — a recovery rate off a trough, which belongs in the EXPLICIT years, never in perpetuity.

Check (b) ROIC x RR implied g from STABLE years only: -2.6%. Burst and loss years are excluded: a reinvestment rate above 100% is financed by new debt, not retained profit, and produces an implied g with no economic meaning.

[Terminal return — the decisive judgement] BOOK invested capital at FY2030E is EGP 1,351mn, giving a book ROIC of 171.6%. That number is arithmetically correct and economically meaningless: it divides today's pounds of profit by 1997 pounds of asset. Taking it would set the reinvestment rate at 2.9% of NOPAT — i.e. 5% perpetual growth bought for almost nothing. REPLACEMENT-COST invested capital is 3.8Mt x USD 130/t x 49.8 = EGP 24,601mn, giving a terminal ROIC of 9.4% and a reinvestment rate of 53.1%. The replacement basis is adopted: growth is only real if someone pays today's price for the capacity that delivers it.

[Terminal] invested capital at FY2030E EGP 1,351mn -> terminal ROIC 9.4%; reinvestment rate = g / ROIC = 5.0% / 9.4% = 53.1%. Terminal NOPAT 2,318 x (1 - 53.1%) / (16.32% - 5.0%) = TV 9,610; discounted on year 5's OWN factor 0.3794 (one date, one price of time) -> PV 3,646.
[TV share] terminal value is 41.0% of enterprise value.

[Ceiling check] terminal g 5.0% against Egypt long-run nominal GDP growth of ~10% (real ~4.5% + 5% inflation). A g at or above that would have the company overtake the whole economy in finite time; 5.0% does not, so no crossover year exists.
[Bridge] PV(FCFF) 5,258 + PV(TV) 3,646 = enterprise value 8,904; + net CASH 5,307 (cash 5,344 less debt 36.8) = equity 14,211 -> EGP 54.49/share
[Relative] normalised EBITDA 2,409 (FY2025 revenue at the 26.5% mid-cycle margin) x 5.0x = EV 12,044; + net cash -> EGP 66.53/share
[Normalised earnings] mid-cycle NOPAT 1,543 + after-tax treasury income = 2,160; x 7.0x -> EGP 57.97/share

[Asset / replacement cost] the market prices SCEM's enterprise at USD 81 per annual tonne of capacity against a USD 130/t build cost — 38% below replacement. At a justified USD 95/t: EV 17,978 + net cash -> EGP 89.28/share. (Book value per share is EGP 27.09 and sustainable return on equity 21.8%, but book is NOT used as a lens here: a plant commissioned in 1997 and carried through a five-fold devaluation has a book value that measures the accounting, not the asset.)
[Synthesis] four lenses: DCF (cash flow) 54.49 | Relative multiples 66.53 | Normalised earnings 57.97 | Asset / replacement cost 89.28
weighted central EGP 62.81 (weights DCF 45%, Relative 20%, Normalised 20%, Asset 15%); field EGP 54.49-89.28 against spot EGP 79.00 (-20.5%)

[Growth destroys value here — the counter-intuitive result, verified not assumed] Raising terminal growth from 3% to 7% LOWERS fair value from EGP 57.28 to EGP 50.50. This is not a model error, it is the arithmetic of ROIC below WACC: terminal return on capital is 9.4% against a terminal cost of capital of 16.3%, so every extra pound of growth must be bought with reinvestment (RR = g / ROIC) that earns less than it costs. For a mature single-plant producer in a market carrying 76Mt of capacity against 54Mt of consumption, that is the correct economic reading: this company creates value by HARVESTING and DISTRIBUTING, not by growing. It is also why the 60% payout assumption is conservative rather than aggressive.
